purpose: Bounded reproduction of configured materialized-view rewriting and independently specified execution results; no LLM, no NL intent truth, no new method.
origin: HR-style synthetic schema inspired by common examples; not claimed to be the official Calcite HrSchema dataset.

table.name: emps
table.extra_constraints: None: do not infer uniqueness, non-NULL salary, group disjointness or current exact cardinality from these small fixtures.

oracle.source: Expected rows authored and checked by direct per-row integer/NULL/grouping logic independently of Calcite Interpreter or planner outputs.
oracle.read_input: Only the four explicitly declared columns and fixture rows.
oracle.result_semantics: Unordered multiset of ordered columns. Duplicate output rows and NULL are retained. SQL defines no ORDER BY in these cases.
oracle.grouping_semantics: All NULL deptno values form one group; empty input produces no GROUP BY rows.
oracle.aggregates: COUNT(*) counts every row. COUNT(expr) excludes NULL. SUM ignores NULL and returns NULL if no non-NULL values. COUNT(DISTINCT expr) counts distinct non-NULL values. Global aggregates return one row even on empty input.
oracle.numeric_comparison: Compare exact mathematical integer values across integral Java numeric representations while recording original classes and output field types separately. Do not stringify NULL, merge NULL and 0, drop duplicates, round arbitrary nonintegral values, or use blanket tolerances. C6's only non-NULL expected value is exactly 180.
oracle.expected_row_order: Recorded for readability only; never require this order.
oracle.independence: Do not generate or adjust these expected values from Calcite output.

evaluation_scope.interpretation: 24 explicitly constructed cases/states, not 24 independent population samples.
evaluation_scope.common_information: Same schema, SQL contracts, view definitions, source snapshot and base-table access for all configurations. Expected rows and theoretical labels are evaluator-only.
evaluation_scope.view_materialization: Compute each V against its corresponding fixture and verify against expected_view_rows before evaluating rewrite outputs; do not build V from target Q answers.
evaluation_scope.capability_label_scope: General algebraic information capability, not a demand that this Calcite rule configuration choose a view and not an assertion about every single special input. Empty/degenerate view values can certify answers in some otherwise insufficient-information cases.
evaluation_scope.negative_case_policy: A correct base fallback is valid. A missed applicable rewrite is configuration coverage, not proof that no rewrite exists.
evaluation_scope.partial_coverage_policy: C8 may require separately enabled union-compensation rules. If unavailable, record UNSUPPORTED_CONFIGURATION_OR_FALLBACK, not a universal planner defect.
evaluation_scope.allowed_validation_actions: Local synthetic tables only. No model calls. Preserve all unsupported/error/timeout/mismatch outcomes.
evaluation_scope.stop_gate: Do not promote a rewrite configuration as safe after a mismatched answer or unverified materialization. Preserve the failed case; never replace it with an easier case.

limitations: Fixed authored SQL, not natural-language parsing or BIRD gold evaluation.
INTEGER-only base measures; DECIMAL, non-integral AVG semantics and overflow need a separately frozen follow-up.
Finite result agreement is not universal query-equivalence proof.
Catalog type declarations and rule configuration are part of the contract; no hidden additional constraints.
View-only feasibility is distinct from optimizer selection and from combined view-plus-base feasibility.
No exact optimizer cost/optimality oracle or speedup guarantee is supplied.
No new algorithm or paper novelty is claimed.

cases.name: bag_preserving_filter
cases.query_sql: SELECT salary FROM emps WHERE deptno = 20

query_columns.name: salary
query_columns.meaning: Every matching employee salary; duplicate rows and NULL retained.

cases.reason: V contains all needed rows and columns; apply deptno = 20 and project salary without DISTINCT.

cases.name: nullable_count_is_not_row_count
cases.view_sql: SELECT deptno, COUNT(salary) AS n FROM emps GROUP BY deptno
cases.query_sql: SELECT deptno, COUNT(*) AS n FROM emps GROUP BY deptno

query_columns.name: deptno
query_columns.meaning: Department grouping key; NULL is a group.

query_columns.name: n
query_columns.meaning: Count every row, including NULL salary.

cases.reason: Adding a NULL-salary row in an existing department changes Q but not V; no exact per-group total-cardinality oracle is provided.

cases.name: missing_measure
cases.view_sql: SELECT deptno, SUM(salary) AS s FROM emps GROUP BY deptno
cases.query_sql: SELECT deptno, SUM(commission) AS s FROM emps GROUP BY deptno

query_columns.name: deptno
query_columns.meaning: Department grouping key; NULL is a group.

query_columns.name: s
query_columns.meaning: Sum non-NULL commissions; NULL when a group has no non-NULL commission.

cases.reason: Changing commission while preserving salary leaves V unchanged but can change Q.

cases.name: lost_grouping_granularity
cases.view_sql: SELECT deptno, SUM(salary) AS s FROM emps GROUP BY deptno
cases.query_sql: SELECT deptno, empid, SUM(salary) AS s FROM emps GROUP BY deptno, empid

query_columns.name: empid
query_columns.meaning: Employee grouping key; no primary-key or uniqueness constraint is supplied.

query_columns.name: s
query_columns.meaning: Sum non-NULL salary in the department/employee group; NULL if all NULL.

cases.reason: The department aggregate does not retain empid or allocation of salary among employees.

cases.name: sum_count_rollup
cases.view_sql: SELECT deptno, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(salary) AS c, SUM(salary) AS s FROM emps GROUP BY deptno
cases.query_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(salary) AS c, SUM(salary) AS s FROM emps

query_columns.name: n
query_columns.meaning: Global row count; 0 for empty input.

query_columns.name: c
query_columns.meaning: Global non-NULL salary count; 0 for empty/all-NULL input.

query_columns.name: s
query_columns.meaning: Global sum ignoring NULL; NULL when no non-NULL salary exists.

cases.reason: SUM(n) and SUM(c), each converted from NULL to 0 on an empty view, plus SUM(s); preserve exactly one global aggregate output row.

cases.name: weighted_average_rollup
cases.view_sql: SELECT deptno, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(salary) AS c, SUM(salary) AS s FROM emps GROUP BY deptno
cases.query_sql: SELECT AVG(salary) AS a FROM emps WHERE deptno IN (10, 20)

query_columns.name: a
query_columns.meaning: Average non-NULL salary of rows with deptno 10 or 20; NULL if no such non-NULL values.

cases.reason: Filter view keys to departments 10 and 20, combine salary sums and non-NULL counts, then divide using the target AVG return semantics; return NULL for zero denominator. Do not average department averages.

oracle_detail.limitation: All non-NULL expected answers here are integral. This batch does not test non-integral AVG rounding/truncation, DECIMAL precision, floating non-associativity or overflow.

cases.name: distinct_count_is_not_additive
cases.view_sql: SELECT deptno, COUNT(DISTINCT salary) AS n FROM emps GROUP BY deptno
cases.query_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT salary) AS n FROM emps

query_columns.name: n
query_columns.meaning: Number of globally distinct non-NULL salaries; 0 for empty/all-NULL input.

cases.reason: Per-group cardinalities omit overlap across groups; no disjointness constraint or stored value sets are available. On base, summing group distinct counts yields 6 but Q is 5.

cases.name: partial_filter_coverage_with_compensation
cases.view_sql: SELECT empid, deptno, salary FROM emps WHERE deptno = 10
cases.query_sql: SELECT empid, deptno, salary FROM emps WHERE deptno IN (10, 20)

query_columns.name: empid
query_columns.meaning: Employee identifier carried through, not deduplicated.

cases.reason: V covers deptno=10 only. UNION ALL with base rows WHERE deptno=20 has disjoint coverage and answers Q; original full recomputation is also legitimate.
